original_value: Wireless multimedia sensor networks (WMSNs) currently face the problem of rapidly decreasing energy due to the acquisition, processing and transmission of massive multimedia data. This decrease in energy affects the life of the network, resulting in higher overhead costs and a deterioration in quality‐of‐service. This study presents a new grouping strategy that somewhat reduces energy reduction problems. The objective is to group cameras in the WMSN according to their field of view. The proposed system begins by searching for all polygons created by the intersection of the two cameras' FoV. Based on the generated surfaces, an ascending hierarchical classification is applied to group cameras with strongly overlapping visions fields. The results obtained with 300 randomly positioned cameras show the effectiveness of the proposed method to minimise redundant detection, reduce energy consumption, increase network life, and reduce network overload.

result.paraphrase: Wireless multimedia sensor networks (WMSNs) are currently challenged by rapidly declining energy levels caused by acquiring, processing, and transmitting large amounts of multimedia data. This energy loss shortens network lifetime, increases overhead costs, and degrades quality of service. This study introduces a new grouping approach that helps alleviate these energy depletion issues. Its goal is to cluster cameras in the WMSN according to their field of view. The proposed method first searches for all polygons formed by the intersection of two cameras’ FoVs. Using the resulting surfaces, an ascending hierarchical classification is then applied to group cameras whose viewing fields overlap strongly. Results from 300 randomly placed cameras demonstrate that the method effectively minimizes redundant detection, lowers energy consumption, extends network lifetime, and reduces network load.
